description: BREAK THE PANEL WALL for the 900us goal: the FP32 Householder panel is 50-83% of EVERY shape and is the universal bottleneck (trailing GEMM is only 14-20% and memory-bound, two workers proved FP8 there is futile). Replace the panel's serial O(n^3) work with TENSOR-CORE GEMMs via per-matrix-routed CholeskyQR2 + Householder reconstruction: for WELL-CONDITIONED matrices (dense majority) compute G=A^T A and Q=A R^-1 on TF32/FP16 tensor cores (2 CholeskyQR passes for O(u) orthogonality; budget admits it at n>=1024 ~2.4e-3, n=2048 ~5e-3, n=4096 ~1e-2), then reconstruct geqrf-exact (H,tau) via the VERIFIED direct column-recurrence HR (recon err 3.8e-15, cheaper than no-pivot LU which capped the earlier FP32-only attempt). Route ILL-conditioned (band/rowscale/nearrank/rankdef/clustered) matrices to the parent's existing FP32 Householder panel. Integrate onto the current best (250a694c); start at n=1024/2048 (loosest budget, biggest panels) and extend to n=512 if accuracy holds. Reconstruction stays FP32. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

CholeskyQR2 + dorhr_col Householder reconstruction (custom lu_panel kernel for modified no-pivot LU of Q); per-matrix a-posteriori orth-gating (orthf>=0.1 -> FP32 panel) routes ill matrices. CORRECT end-to-end (validate PASS all 22 shapes; n=1024 dense/nearrank/rankdef/clustered/mixed all pass with factor_scaled ~0.008-0.012<<20). REGRESSION: torch cholesky_ex+solve_triangular are the cuSOLVER cliff; nsys: lu_panel_kernel 39.6%, cholesky/trsm ~15%, and the GEMMs are cutlass3x_sm100_SIMT_sgemm (FP32=SIMT, NOT tensor-core) ~25%. n=1024 shapes 9k->60k us (fast-mode). geomean 4405->6990 (fast bimodal mode).

Restructure recon to factor ONLY cb x cb diagonal block in-kernel (lu_diag) + torch trsm L21/U12 + bmm Schur. Still correct (validate-equiv probe all pass). REGRESSION: 32 torch solve_triangular/factorization hit the cuSOLVER trsm cliff. This run landed in SLOW bimodal mode (~2x ALL shapes incl unchanged n=512/4096), geomean 12952us inflated vs trial-1 fast-mode 6990. Lesson: torch trsm/cholesky=cliff; need in-kernel L21 (trial1 lu_panel) AND tensor-core (TF32) GEMMs -- FP32 GEMM is SIMT on B200.

lu_diag kernel now inverts L11/U11 in SMEM (back/forward subst) so the recon's L21/U12/Schur are ALL batched bmm GEMMs -- ZERO cuSOLVER trsm in the reconstruction. Correct (all n=1024 cases pass). MIN-of-3 = 12879us but GPU stuck in SLOW bimodal mode (shape3 n512=17670-17683 = ~2x fast-mode 7842; 3 reads 12877/12879/12883). vs trial-1 fast 6990: bimodal ratio ~1.84x so slow-equiv parent~8100, trial1~12860, trial3~12879 => trial3 ~= trial1 geomean. nsys (slow-mode, big StdDev): cost now SPREAD -- Gram FP32-SIMT GEMMs, batch_trsm_right (CholeskyQR Q=A*R^-1, NOT yet replaced) 10%, potrf cholesky 10%, lu_diag down to 5%, ~20% elementwise (per-panel Schur subtract+tril/triu+where). The all-GEMM recon removed the trial-1 40% lu_panel bottleneck.

Built CholeskyQR2 + dorhr_col Householder reconstruction for n=1024 end-to-end; CORRECT (validate PASS all 22 shapes; n=1024 dense/cond4/nearrank/rankdef/clustered/mixed all pass, factor_scaled ~0.008-0.012<<20). dorhr_col VERIFIED: factor Q (orthonormal) with the modified no-pivot LU (D=-sign(modified pivot), |pivot|>=1), L=reflectors, tau=|U_diag|, R_out=diag(D)*R_chol; matches geqrf ~2e-6. Custom kernel lu_diag factors+inverts the cb=64 diagonal block in SMEM so the recon's L21/U12/Schur are ALL batched bmm (ZERO cuSOLVER trsm in recon). Per-matrix a-posteriori orth-gating (orthf=|Q^TQ-I|_1>=0.1 -> FP32 panel; well ~1e-5 vs ill >=1e3, 8-order gap) is seed-safe.

MEASURED (MODE-CONTROLLED, both slow-bimodal): PARENT n=1024 dense shape4=32126us vs TRIAL-3=83491us => 2.6x SLOWER on the shapes I changed. (Geomean parent 13499 vs trial3 12866 is bimodal NOISE on the UNCHANGED n=512 shape: parent hit 26598 vs trial3 17678 for identical n=512 code.) Trial-1 fast-mode geomean 6990 vs parent fast 4405.

WHY SLOWER (rigorously established, not pre-judged): the brief premise 'move O(n^3) panel onto tensor cores' does NOT hold at FP32 accuracy on B200. (1) The Gram A^T A MUST be FP32 (TF32 Gram FAILS the checker; 2pass TF32 fails) and FP32 GEMM is cutlass3x_sm100_SIMT_sgemm -- NOT tensor-core. (2) FP16x3 error-corrected Gram = only 1.5x faster AND rel-err 4.5e-4 makes the borderline cond-2 Gram non-SPD -> NaN. (3) cuSOLVER cholesky_ex (~3.2ms) + solve_triangular (Q=A*R^-1, ~3.2ms) are the dispatch cliff. (4) ~20% Python-orchestration elementwise (per-panel Schur subtract+tril/triu+where). nsys trial-3: cost SPREAD across Gram-SIMT, batch_trsm_right 10%, potrf 10%, lu_diag 5%, elementwise 20%. The parent's ONE fused tuned FP32 panel beats this multi-op FP32-SIMT decomposition.

STILL OPEN (did not reach): (a) custom batched Cholesky-INVERSE kernel (chol_diag, same panel+GEMM+SMEM-inverse pattern as my validated lu_diag) to replace BOTH cholesky_ex AND solve_triangular -- the two remaining cuSOLVER cliffs (~20% combined); this is the brief's 'then optimize' step I did not finish. (b) fuse the per-panel Schur via baddbmm + raise MAXCB_LU to cut panel count (16->8) and elementwise overhead. (c) n=2048 (looser budget 5e-3) was never attempted -- it may tolerate the precision better and has a bigger panel to amortize. (d) the deeper question for the manager: even with all cliffs removed the FLOOR is FP32-SIMT Gram(~0.6ms)+custom-chol+custom-trsm+LU; whether that beats the parent's 9ms(fast)/32ms(slow) n=1024 panel is unproven -- needs the full custom-kernel suite built. Benchmark was stuck in SLOW bimodal mode the entire trial-3 window (5 reads 12866-12883), so fast-mode trial-3 was never captured for a clean fast-vs-fast number.
